  36def generateAtomsXYZ(struc, rmax=30.0, strucIdxs=[0], square=False):
  37    """Generate array of atomic Cartesian coordinates from a given structure.
  38
  39    Args:
  40        struc (diffpy.Structure object): provides lattice parameters and unit
  41            cell of the desired structure
  42        rmax (float): largest distance from central atom that should be
  43            included
  44        strucIdxs (python list): list of integers giving indices of magnetic
  45            atoms in the unit cell
  46        square (boolean): if not True, atoms within a given radius from the
  47            origin will be returned; if True, then the full grid will be
  48            returned rather than just a spherical selection.
  49
  50    Returns:
  51        numpy array of triples giving the Cartesian coordinates of all the
  52            magnetic atoms. Atom closest to the origin placed first in array.
  53
  54    Note: If square = True, this may have problems for structures that have
  55        a several distorted unit cell (i.e. highly non-orthorhombic).
  56    """
  57    if not square:
  58        magAtoms = struc[strucIdxs]
  59        bc = BondCalculator(rmax=rmax + np.linalg.norm(struc.lattice.stdbase.sum(axis=1)))
  60        bc.setPairMask(0, 'all', True, others=False)
  61        bc(magAtoms)
  62        r0 = struc.xyz_cartn[strucIdxs[0]]
  63        atoms = np.vstack([r0, r0 + bc.directions[bc.sites0 == 0]])
  64
  65    else:
  66        ### generate the coordinates of each unit cell
  67        lat = struc.lattice
  68        unitcell = lat.stdbase
  69        cellwithatoms = struc.xyz_cartn[np.array(strucIdxs)]
  70        dim1 = int(np.round(rmax / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[0])))
  71        dim2 = int(np.round(rmax / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[1])))
  72        dim3 = int(np.round(rmax / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[2])))
  73        ocoords = np.mgrid[-dim1:dim1 + 1, -dim2:dim2 + 1, -dim3:dim3 + 1].transpose().ravel().reshape(
  74            (2 * dim1 + 1) * (2 * dim2 + 1) * (2 * dim3 + 1), 3)
  75        latos = np.dot(ocoords, unitcell)
  76
  77        ### rearrange latos array so that [0, 0, 0] is the first one (for convenience)
  78        latos[np.where(np.all(latos == [0, 0, 0], axis=1))] = latos[0]
  79        latos[0] = np.array([0, 0, 0])
  80
  81        ### create list of all atomic positions
  82        atoms = np.empty([len(latos) * len(cellwithatoms), 3])
  83        index = 0
  84        for lato in latos:
  85            for atompos in cellwithatoms:
  86                atoms[index] = lato + atompos
  87                index += 1
  88
  89    return atoms

  92def generateSpinsXYZ(struc, atoms=np.array([[]]), kvecs=np.array([[0, 0, 0]]),
  93                     basisvecs=np.array([[0, 0, 1]]), origin=np.array([0, 0, 0]),
  94                     avgmom=np.array([0, 0, 0])):
  95    """Generate array of 3-vectors representing the spins in a structure.
  96
  97    Args:
  98        struc (diffpy.Structure object): provides lattice parameters and unit
  99            cell of the desired structure
 100        atoms (numpy array): list of atomic coordinates of all the magnetic
 101            atoms of a given magnetic species in the structure
 102        avgmom (numpy array): three-vector giving the average moment for the
 103            magnetic species.
 104        kvecs (numpy array): list of three-vectors giving the propagation
 105            vector(s) of the magnetic structure
 106        basisvecs (numpy array): list of three-vectors describing the spin
 107            located at the spin origin.
 108        origin (numpy array): Cartesian coordinates specifying the origin
 109            to be used when calculating the phases of the spins.
 110
 111    Returns:
 112        numpy array of triples giving the spin vectors of all the magnetic
 113            atoms, in the same order as the atoms array provided as input.
 114
 115    """
 116
 117    lat = struc.lattice
 118    rlat = lat.reciprocal()
 119    (astar, bstar, cstar) = (rlat.cartesian((1, 0, 0)), rlat.cartesian((0, 1, 0)),
 120                             rlat.cartesian((0, 0, 1)))
 121    i = 1j
 122
 123    spins = 0 * atoms
 124    cspins = 0 * atoms + 0j * atoms
 125    if len(np.array(kvecs).shape) == 1:
 126        kvecs = [kvecs]
 127    if len(np.array(basisvecs).shape) == 1:
 128        basisvecs = [basisvecs]
 129    for idx, kvec in enumerate(kvecs):
 130        kcart = kvec[0] * astar + kvec[1] * bstar + kvec[2] * cstar
 131        phasefac = np.exp(-2.0 * np.pi * i * np.dot(atoms - origin, kcart))
 132        cspins += basisvecs[idx] * phasefac[:, np.newaxis]
 133    cspins += avgmom
 134    spins = np.real(cspins)
 135
 136    if np.abs(np.imag(cspins)).max() > 0.0001:
 137        print((np.abs(np.imag(cspins)).max()))
 138        print('Warning: basis vectors resulted in complex spins.')
 139        print('Imaginary parts have been discarded.')
 140
 141    return spins

 144def generateFromUnitCell(unitcell, atombasis, spinbasis, rmax=30.0):
 145    """Generate array of atomic Cartesian coordinates from a given structure.
 146
 147    Args:
 148        unitcell (numpy array): np.array([avec, bvec, cvec])
 149        atombasis (numpy array): gives positions of magnetic atoms in
 150            fractional coordinates; np.array([pos1, pos2, pos3, ...])
 151        spinbasis (numpy array): gives orientations of the magnetic moments
 152            in the unit cell, in the same order as atombasis
 153        rmax (float): largest distance from central atom that should be
 154            included
 155
 156    Returns:
 157        atoms = numpy array of triples giving the Cartesian coordinates of all
 158              the magnetic atoms. Atom closest to the origin placed first in
 159              array.
 160        spins = numpy array of triples giving the Cartesian coordinates of all
 161              the spins in the structure, in the same order as atoms.
 162
 163    Note: This will only work well for structures that can be expressed with a
 164        unit cell that is close to orthorhombic or higher symmetry.
 165    """
 166    if len(np.array(atombasis).shape) == 1:
 167        atombasis = [atombasis]
 168    if len(np.array(spinbasis).shape) == 1:
 169        spinbasis = [spinbasis]
 170    cellwithatoms = np.dot(atombasis, unitcell)  ### check this
 171    radius = rmax + 15.0
 172    dim1 = int(np.round(radius / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[0])))
 173    dim2 = int(np.round(radius / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[1])))
 174    dim3 = int(np.round(radius / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[2])))
 175
 176    ### generate the coordinates of each unit cell
 177    ocoords = np.mgrid[-dim1:dim1 + 1, -dim2:dim2 + 1, -dim3:dim3 + 1].transpose().ravel().reshape(
 178        (2 * dim1 + 1) * (2 * dim2 + 1) * (2 * dim3 + 1), 3)
 179    latos = np.dot(ocoords, unitcell)
 180
 181    ### select points within a desired radius from origin
 182    latos = latos[np.where(np.apply_along_axis(np.linalg.norm, 1, latos) <=
 183                           (rmax + np.linalg.norm(unitcell.sum(axis=1))))]
 184
 185    ## rearrange latos array so that [0, 0, 0] is the first one (for convenience)
 186    latos[np.where(np.all(latos == [0, 0, 0], axis=1))] = latos[0]
 187    latos[0] = np.array([0, 0, 0])
 188
 189    ### create list of all atomic positions
 190    atoms = np.empty([len(latos) * len(cellwithatoms), 3])
 191    spins = np.empty_like(atoms)
 192    index = 0
 193    for lato in latos:
 194        for j, atompos in enumerate(cellwithatoms):
 195            atoms[index] = lato + atompos
 196            spins[index] = spinbasis[j]
 197            index += 1
 198    return atoms, spins

 419def spinsFromAtoms(magstruc, positions, fractional=True, returnIdxs=False):
 420    """Return the spin vectors corresponding to specified atomic
 421       positions.
 422
 423    Args:
 424        magstruc: MagSpecies or MagStructure object containing atoms and spins
 425        positions (list or array): atomic positions for which the
 426            corresponding spins should be returned.
 427        fractional (boolean): set as True if the atomic positions are in
 428            fractional coordinates of the crystallographic lattice
 429            vectors.
 430        returnIdxs (boolean): if True, the indices of the spins will also be
 431            returned.
 432    Returns:
 433        Array consisting of the spins corresponding to the atomic positions.
 434    """
 435    if len(np.array(positions).shape) == 1:
 436        positions = [positions]
 437    spins = []
 438    idxs = []
 439    badlist = []
 440    for pos in positions:
 441        if fractional:
 442            pos = magstruc.struc.lattice.cartesian(pos)
 443        mask = np.all(np.round(magstruc.atoms, decimals=4) ==
 444                      np.round(pos, decimals=4), axis=1)
 445        goodspins = magstruc.spins[mask]
 446        goodidxs = np.where(mask)[0]
 447        if len(goodspins) == 1:
 448            spins.append(goodspins[0])
 449            idxs.append(goodidxs[0])
 450        elif len(goodspins) > 1:
 451            print('Warning: duplicate atoms in structure')
 452            spins.append(goodspins)
 453            idxs.append(goodidxs)
 454        elif len(goodspins) == 0:
 455            spins.append([])
 456            idxs.append([])
 457            badlist.append(pos)
 458    if len(badlist) > 0:
 459        print('The following atomic positions do not correspond to a spin:')
 460        for bad in badlist:
 461            if fractional:
 462                bad = magstruc.struc.lattice.fractional(pos)
 463            print(bad)
 464    if not returnIdxs:
 465        return spins
 466    else:
 467        return spins, idxs
 468
 469
 470def atomsFromSpins(magstruc, spinvecs, fractional=True, returnIdxs=False):
 471    """Return the atomic positions corresponding to specified spins.
 472
 473    Args:
 474        magstruc: MagSpecies or MagStructure object containing atoms and spins
 475        spinvecs (list or array): spin vectors for which the
 476            corresponding atoms should be returned.
 477        fractional (boolean): set as True if the atomic positions are to be
 478            returned as fractional coordinates of the crystallographic lattice
 479            vectors.
 480        returnIdxs (boolean): if True, the indices of the atoms will also be
 481            returned.
 482
 483    Returns:
 484        List of arrays of atoms corresponding to the spins.
 485    """
 486    if len(np.array(spinvecs).shape) == 1:
 487        spinvecs = [spinvecs]
 488    atoms = []
 489    idxs = []
 490    badlist = []
 491    for spin in spinvecs:
 492        mask = np.all(np.round(magstruc.spins, decimals=5) ==
 493                      np.round(spin, decimals=5), axis=1)
 494        goodatoms = magstruc.atoms[mask]
 495        goodidxs = np.where(mask)[0]
 496        if fractional:
 497            goodatoms = magstruc.struc.lattice.fractional(goodatoms)
 498        atoms.append(goodatoms)
 499        idxs.append(goodidxs)
 500        if len(goodidxs) == 0:
 501            badlist.append(spin)
 502    if len(badlist) > 0:
 503        print('The following spins were not found in the structure:')
 504        for bad in badlist:
 505            print(bad)
 506    if not returnIdxs:
 507        return atoms
 508    else:
 509        return atoms, idxs
 510

 512def visualizeSpins(atoms, spins):
 513    """Set up a 3d plot showing an arrangement of spins.
 514
 515    Args:
 516        atoms (numpy array): array of atomic positions of spins to be
 517            visualized.
 518        spins (numpy array): array of spin vectors in same order as atoms.
 519
 520    Returns:
 521        matplotlib figure object with a quiver plot on 3d axes.
 522    """
 523    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
 524    from mpl_toolkits.mplot3d import Axes3D
 525
 526    xx, yy, zz = np.transpose(atoms)
 527    uu, vv, ww = np.transpose(spins)
 528
 529    fig = plt.figure()
 530    ax = fig.add_subplot(111, projection='3d')
 531    for i in range(len(xx)):
 532        x, y, z = 1.0 * xx[i], 1.0 * yy[i], 1.0 * zz[i]
 533        u, v, w = 1.0 * uu[i], 1.0 * vv[i], 1.0 * ww[i]
 534        ax.quiver(x, y, z, u, v, w, pivot='middle') # I think this gives the correct arrow length
 535        #lngth = np.sqrt(u ** 2 + v ** 2 + w ** 2)
 536        #ax.quiver(x, y, z, u, v, w, length=lngth, pivot='middle')
 537
 538    xmin, xmax = ax.get_xlim3d()
 539    ax.set_xlim3d(np.min((-1, xmin)), np.max((1, xmax)))
 540    ymin, ymax = ax.get_ylim3d()
 541    ax.set_ylim3d(np.min((-1, ymin)), np.max((1, ymax)))
 542    zmin, zmax = ax.get_zlim3d()
 543    ax.set_zlim3d(np.min((-1, zmin)), np.max((1, zmax)))
 544
 545    return fig

 548def findAtomIndices(magstruc, atomList):
 549    """Return list of indices corresponding to input list of atomic coordinates.
 550
 551    Args:
 552        atomList (numpy array of atomic coordinates)
 553
 554    Returns:
 555        List of indices corresponding to the atomList.
 556    """
 557    if len(np.array(atomList).shape) == 1:
 558        atomList = [atomList]
 559    indices = []
 560    x, y, z = magstruc.atoms.transpose()
 561    allIdxs = np.arange(len(x))
 562    for idx, atom in enumerate(atomList):
 563        xa, ya, za = atom[0], atom[1], atom[2]
 564        maskx = (np.abs(x - xa) < 0.01)
 565        masky = (np.abs(y - ya) < 0.01)
 566        maskz = (np.abs(z - za) < 0.01)
 567        match = allIdxs[np.logical_and(maskx, np.logical_and(masky, maskz))]
 568        if len(match) == 0:
 569            print(('Warning: atom with index ' + str(idx) + ' in atomList could not'))
 570            print('be found in the MagStructure, so the index -1 has been')
 571            print('returned instead.')
 572            indices.append(-1)
 573        if len(match) == 1:
 574            indices.append(match[0])
 575        if len(match) > 1:
 576            print(('Warning: ' + str(len(match)) + ' atoms matching index ' + str(idx)))
 577            print('have been found in the MagStructure, so just the first index has')
 578            print('been returned.')
 579            indices.append(match[0])
 580
 581    return indices

 584def getStrucFromPDFgui(fileName, fitIdx=0, phaseIdx=0):
 585    """Extract the refined atomic structure from a PDFgui project file.
 586
 587    Args:
 588        fileName (str): path to the .ddp file containing the fit
 589        fitIdx (int): index of fit in .ddp file from which the refined
 590             structure is to be extracted. Default is 0.
 591        phaseIdx (int): index of phase within the specified fit for
 592             which the refined structure is to be extracted. Default
 593             is 0.
 594
 595    Returns:
 596        struc (diffpy.Structure object): Refined atomic structure.
 597    """
 598    if fileName[-4:] == '.ddp':
 599        from diffpy.pdfgui import tui
 600        prj = tui.LoadProject(fileName)
 601        try:
 602            fit = prj.getFits()[fitIdx]
 603        except IndexError:
 604            print('Fit index does not correspond to any fit in your')
 605            print('PDFgui project.')
 606            struc = []
 607            return struc
 608        try:
 609            struc = prj.getPhases([fit])[phaseIdx]
 610            struc = struc.refined
 611        except IndexError:
 612            print('Phase index does not correspond to any phase in your')
 613            print('specified fit in the PDFgui project.')
 614            struc = []
 615        return struc
 616    else:
 617        print('Please provide a PDFgui project file (.ddp extension)')
 618        return []

 621def jCalc(q, params=[0.2394, 26.038, 0.4727, 12.1375, 0.3065, 3.0939, -0.01906],
 622          j2=False):
 623    """Calculate the magnetic form factor j0.
 624
 625    This method for calculating the magnetic form factor is based on the
 626    approximate empirical forms based on the tables by Brown, consisting of
 627    the sum of 3 Gaussians and a constant.
 628
 629    Args:
 630        q (numpy array): 1-d grid of momentum transfer on which the form
 631            factor is to be computed
 632        params (python list): provides the 7 numerical coefficients. The
 633            default is an average form factor of 3d j0 approximations.
 634        j2 (boolean): if True, calculate the j2 approximation for orbital
 635            angular momentum contributions
 636
 637    Returns:
 638        numpy array with same shape as q giving the magnetic form factor j0 or j2.
 639    """
 640    [A, a, B, b, C, c, D] = params
 641    if j2:
 642        return (A * np.exp(-a * (q / 4 / np.pi) ** 2) + B * np.exp(-b * (q / 4 / np.pi) ** 2) + C * np.exp(
 643            -c * (q / 4 / np.pi) ** 2) + D) * (q / 4.0 / np.pi) ** 2
 644    else:
 645        return A * np.exp(-a * (q / 4 / np.pi) ** 2) + B * np.exp(-b * (q / 4 / np.pi) ** 2) + C * np.exp(
 646            -c * (q / 4 / np.pi) ** 2) + D
 647

 649def cv(x1, y1, x2, y2, align=False, normalize=False):
 650    """Perform the convolution of two functions and give the correct output.
 651
 652
 653    Args:
 654        x1 (numpy array): independent variable of first function; must be in
 655            ascending order
 656        y1 (numpy array): dependent variable of first function
 657        x2 (numpy array): independent variable of second function; must have
 658            same grid spacing as x1
 659        y2 (numpy array): dependent variable of second function
 660        align (boolean): if True, output grid will be identical to input x1, y1
 661        normalize (boolean): if True, the output will be scaled to match y1
 662
 663    Returns:
 664        xcv (numpy array): independent variable of convoluted function, has
 665            dimension len(x1) + len(x2) - 1 unless align option us used.
 666
 667        ycv (numpy array): convolution of y1 and y2, same shape as xcv
 668
 669    """
 670    dx = x1[1] - x1[0]
 671    ycv = dx * convolve(y1, y2, 'full')
 672    xcv = np.linspace(x1[0] + x2[0], x1[-1] + x2[-1], len(ycv))
 673    if align: # align output with the x1 and y1 input grids
 674        lb = x1[0] - 0.5 * dx
 675        ub = x1[-1] + 0.5 * dx
 676        mask = np.logical_and(xcv > lb, xcv < ub)
 677        ycv = ycv[mask]
 678        xcv = xcv[mask]
 679    if normalize: # normalize y1 to its original scale
 680        try:
 681            ycv /= np.trapz(y2, x2)
 682        except AttributeError: # flexibility for different numpy versions
 683            ycv /= np.trapezoid(y2, x2) 
 684    return xcv, ycv
 685

 687def fourierTransform(q, fq, rmin=0.0, rmax=50.0, rstep=0.1):  # requires even q-grid
 688    """Compute the Fourier transform of a function.
 689
 690    This method uses the FFT algorithm and returns correctly spaced x and
 691    y arrays on an even and specifiable grid. The input grid must be evenly
 692    spaced.
 693
 694    Args:
 695        q (numpy array): independent variable for function to be transformed
 696        fq (numpy array): dependent variable for function to be transformed
 697        rmin (float, default = 0.0): min value of conjugate independent variable
 698            grid
 699        rmax (float, default = 50.0): maximum value of conjugate independent
 700            variable grid
 701        rstep (float, default = 0.1): grid spacing for conjugate independent
 702            variable
 703
 704    Returns:
 705        r (numpy array): independent variable grid for transformed quantity
 706
 707        fr (numpy array): Fourier transform of fq (complex)
 708    """
 709    lostep = int(np.ceil((rmin - 1e-8) / rstep))
 710    histep = int(np.floor((rmax + 1e-8) / rstep)) + 1
 711    r = np.arange(lostep, histep) * rstep
 712    qstep = q[1] - q[0]
 713    if (q[0] - 0.01 * qstep) > 0:
 714        nn = int(np.round(q[0] / qstep))
 715        addme = np.linspace(0.0, q[0] - qstep, nn)
 716        q = np.concatenate((addme, q))
 717        fq = np.concatenate((0.0 * addme, fq))
 718    qmaxrstep = np.pi / rstep
 719    nin = len(q)
 720    nbase = max([nin, histep, qmaxrstep / qstep])
 721    nlog2 = int(np.ceil(np.log2(nbase)))
 722    nout = 2 ** nlog2
 723    qmaxdb = 2 * nout * qstep
 724    yindb = np.concatenate((fq, np.zeros(2 * nout - nin)))
 725    cyoutdb = np.fft.ifft(yindb) * np.sqrt(2 / np.pi) * qmaxdb
 726    frdb = cyoutdb
 727    rstepfine = 2 * np.pi / qmaxdb
 728    rfine = np.arange(nout) * rstepfine
 729    frfine = frdb[:nout]
 730    frr = np.interp(r, rfine, np.real(frfine))
 731    fri = np.interp(r, rfine, np.imag(frfine))
 732    if r[0] + 0.0001 * rstep < 0:
 733        nn = int(np.round(-r[0] / rstep))
 734        frr[:nn] = 1.0 * frr[2 * nn:nn:-1]
 735        fri[:nn] = -1.0 * fri[2 * nn:nn:-1]
 736    fr = frr + 1j * fri
 737    return r, fr
 738
 739
 740def cosTransform(q, fq, rmin=0.0, rmax=50.0, rstep=0.1):  # requires even q-grid
 741    """Compute the cosine Fourier transform of a function.
 742
 743    This method uses the FFT algorithm and returns correctly spaced x and
 744    y arrays on an even and specifiable grid. The input grid must be evenly
 745    spaced.
 746
 747    Args:
 748        q (numpy array): independent variable for function to be transformed
 749        fq (numpy array): dependent variable for function to be transformed
 750        rmin (float, default = 0.0): min value of conjugate independent variable
 751            grid
 752        rmax (float, default = 50.0): maximum value of conjugate independent
 753            variable grid
 754        rstep (float, default = 0.1): grid spacing for conjugate independent
 755            variable
 756
 757    Returns:
 758        r (numpy array): independent variable grid for transformed quantity
 759
 760        fr (numpy array): cosine Fourier transform of fq
 761    """
 762    r, fr = fourierTransform(q, fq, rmin, rmax, rstep)
 763    fr = np.real(fr)
 764    return r, fr
 765
 766
 767def sinTransform(q, fq, rmin=0.0, rmax=50.0, rstep=0.1):  # requires even q-grid
 768    """Compute the sine Fourier transform of a function.
 769
 770    This method uses direct integration rather than an FFT and doesn't require
 771    an even grid. The grid for the Fourier transform is even and specifiable.
 772
 773    Args:
 774        q (numpy array): independent variable for function to be transformed
 775        fq (numpy array): dependent variable for function to be transformed
 776        rmin (float, default = 0.0): min value of conjugate independent variable
 777            grid
 778        rmax (float, default = 50.0): maximum value of conjugate independent
 779            variable grid
 780        rstep (float, default = 0.1): grid spacing for conjugate independent
 781            variable
 782
 783    Returns:
 784        r (numpy array): independent variable grid for transformed quantity
 785
 786        fr (numpy array): sine Fourier transform of fq
 787    """
 788    r, fr = fourierTransform(q, fq, rmin, rmax, rstep)
 789    fr = np.imag(fr)
 790    return r, fr
 791
 792
 793def cosTransformDirectIntegration(q, fq, rmin=0.0, rmax=50.0, rstep=0.1):  # does not require even q-grid
 794    """Compute the cosine Fourier transform of a function.
 795
 796    This method uses direct integration rather than an FFT and doesn't require
 797    an even grid. The grid for the Fourier transform is even and specifiable.
 798
 799    Args:
 800        q (numpy array): independent variable for function to be transformed
 801        fq (numpy array): dependent variable for function to be transformed
 802        rmin (float, default = 0.0): min value of conjugate independent variable
 803            grid
 804        rmax (float, default = 50.0): maximum value of conjugate independent
 805            variable grid
 806        rstep (float, default = 0.1): grid spacing for conjugate independent
 807            variable
 808
 809    Returns:
 810        r (numpy array): independent variable grid for transformed quantity
 811
 812        fr (numpy array): cosine Fourier transform of fq
 813    """
 814    lostep = int(np.ceil((rmin - 1e-8) / rstep))
 815    histep = int(np.floor((rmax + 1e-8) / rstep)) + 1
 816    r = np.arange(lostep, histep) * rstep
 817    qrmat = np.outer(r, q)
 818    integrand = fq * np.cos(qrmat)
 819    try:
 820        fr = np.sqrt(2.0 / np.pi) * np.trapz(integrand, q)
 821    except AttributeError: # flexibility for different numpy versions
 822        fr = np.sqrt(2.0 / np.pi) * np.trapezoid(integrand, q)
 823    return r, fr
 824
 825
 826def sinTransformDirectIntegration(q, fq, rmin=0.0, rmax=50.0, rstep=0.1):  # does not require even q-grid
 827    """Compute the sine Fourier transform of a function.
 828
 829    This method uses direct integration rather than an FFT and doesn't require
 830    an even grid. The grid for the Fourier transform is even and specifiable.
 831
 832    Args:
 833        q (numpy array): independent variable for function to be transformed
 834        fq (numpy array): dependent variable for function to be transformed
 835        rmin (float, default = 0.0): min value of conjugate independent variable
 836            grid
 837        rmax (float, default = 50.0): maximum value of conjugate independent
 838            variable grid
 839        rstep (float, default = 0.1): grid spacing for conjugate independent
 840            variable
 841
 842    Returns:
 843        r (numpy array): independent variable grid for transformed quantity
 844
 845        fr (numpy array): cosine Fourier transform of fq
 846    """
 847    lostep = int(np.ceil((rmin - 1e-8) / rstep))
 848    histep = int(np.floor((rmax + 1e-8) / rstep)) + 1
 849    r = np.arange(lostep, histep) * rstep
 850    qrmat = np.outer(r, q)
 851    integrand = fq * np.sin(qrmat)
 852    try:
 853        fr = np.sqrt(2.0 / np.pi) * np.trapz(integrand, q)
 854    except AttributeError: # flexibility for different numpy versions
 855        fr = np.sqrt(2.0 / np.pi) * np.trapezoid(integrand, q)
 856    return r, fr

 859def getStdUnc(fitResult, data, dataErr=None, numConstraints=0):
 860    """Return the standard uncertainty of refined parameters.
 861    This method is based on the scipy.optimize.least_squares routine.
 862
 863    Args:
 864        fitResult: Output from scipy.optimize.least_squares routine
 865        data (numpy array): The data against which the fit is performed
 866        dataErr (numpy array): Experimental uncertainties on the data points
 867            (set to unity if not provided)
 868        numConstraints (int): Number of constraints used in the model
 869    Returns:
 870        pUnc (numpy array): standard uncertainties of the refined parameters.
 871        chisq (float): Value of chi^2 for the fit.
 872    """
 873    if dataErr is None:
 874        dataErr = np.ones_like(data)
 875    weights = 1.0 / dataErr ** 2
 876    Rw = np.sqrt((fitResult.fun ** 2).sum() / (data ** 2 * weights).sum())
 877    numParams = len(fitResult.x)
 878    Rexp = np.sqrt((data.shape[0] - numParams + numConstraints) / (data ** 2 * weights).sum())
 879    j = fitResult.jac
 880    jac = np.dot(j.transpose(), j)
 881    cov = np.linalg.inv(jac) * Rw ** 2 / Rexp ** 2
 882    pUnc = np.sqrt(cov.diagonal())
 883    chisq = Rw ** 2 / Rexp ** 2
 884    return pUnc, chisq
 885
 886
 887def optimizedSubtraction(rhigh, dhigh, rlow, dlow, p0=[0.999, 0.1], print_output=False):
 888    '''
 889    This routine stretches and broadens a low-temperature atomic PDF fit residual
 890    to match a high-temperature fit residual as closely as possible. The idea is
 891    to minimize thermal effects when doing the temperature subtraction so that
 892    the mDPF can be obtained as cleanly as possible.
 893
 894    rhigh = r array for high-temperature atomic PDF fit residual
 895    dhigh = high-temperature atomic PDF fit residual
 896    rlow = r array for low-temperature atomic PDF fit residual
 897    dlow = low-temperature atomic PDF fit residual
 898    p0 = initial guesses for stretching and broadening factors; [0.999, 0.1]
 899        by default.
 900    print_output (bool): True if the optimized stretching and broadening factors
 901        should be printed. False by default.
 902    Note: the high- and low-temperature fits should be over the same r range
 903    '''
 904
 905    def gaussianSmooth(x, y, sig=0.1):
 906        dr = np.mean((x - np.roll(x, 1))[1:])
 907        rs = np.arange(-10, 10, dr)
 908        s = np.exp(-rs ** 2 / 2.0 / sig ** 2)
 909        xsmooth, ysmooth = cv(x, y, rs, s)
 910        try:
 911            ysmooth /= np.trapz(s, rs)
 912        except AttributeError: # flexibility for different numpy versions
 913            ysmooth /= np.trapezoid(s, rs)
 914        msk = np.logical_and(xsmooth > (x.min() - 0.5 * dr), xsmooth < (x.max() + 0.5 * dr))
 915        return ysmooth[msk]
 916
 917    def residual(p, x, y, ycomp):
 918        stretch, width = p
 919        newx = stretch * x
 920        newy = np.interp(newx, x, y)
 921        newy = gaussianSmooth(newx, newy, width)
 922        msk = (x <= x.max() / stretch)
 923        return ycomp[msk] - newy[msk]
 924
 925    opt = least_squares(residual, p0, args=(rlow, dlow, dhigh))
 926    if print_output:
 927        print(opt.x)
 928    stretch = opt.x[0]
 929    msk = (rlow <= rlow.max() / stretch)
 930    newdllow = dhigh[msk] - residual(opt.x, rlow, dlow, dhigh)
 931    diff = newdllow - dhigh[msk]
 932    return rhigh[msk], diff
 933
 934
 935def smoothData(xdata, ydata, qCutoff, func='sinc', gaussHeight=0.01):
 936    """Smooth out high-frequency contributions from the data.
 937
 938    This method performs a convolution in real space to simulate a truncation
 939    in reciprocal space. This is motivated by the fact that high-frequency
 940    noise can sometimes obscure the lower-frequency mPDF signal when the mPDF
 941    is collected together with the nuclear PDF. This high-frequency noise comes
 942    from scattering intensity at high q that cannot possibly come from magnetic
 943    scattering, due to the strong suppression from the magnetic form factor.
 944    To better isolate the mPDF from this high-frequency noise, one could
 945    truncate the Fourier transfrom at some cutoff q value beyond which the
 946    magnetic scattering is negligible (e.g. where the square of the magnetic
 947    form factor is reduced to 1% of its original value). This can be done by
 948    multiplying the scattering in q-space by a "window function" that is equal
 949    to unity for q between 0 and the cutoff value and 0 outside this window.
 950    By the convolution theorem, this is equivalent to convoluting the full
 951    Fourier transform in real space with a sinc function. Alternatively, one
 952    could multiply the scattering in q-space by a Guassian function which is
 953    reduced to some small amplitude at the desired cutoff q value.  This is
 954    equivalent to a convolution in real space with another Gaussian function.
 955    The former method is recommended because it will generally be more
 956    physically justifiable.
 957
 958    Args:
 959        xdata: numpy array containing the independent variable of the data
 960            to be smoothed.
 961        ydata: numpy array containing the dependent variable; this array will
 962            be smoothed.
 963        qCutoff: q value beyond which all contributions will be ignored.
 964        func: string specifying the type of real-space convolution function,
 965            either 'sinc' or 'gaussian' (see previous discussion).
 966        gaussHeight: float specifying what the height of the q-space Gaussian
 967            function should be at the specified value of qCutoff.
 968
 969    Returns:
 970        Numpy array containing the smoothed version of ydata.
 971    """
 972    dr = np.mean((xdata - np.roll(xdata, 1))[1:])
 973    rs = np.arange(-10, 10, dr)
 974    if func == 'sinc':
 975        s = np.sinc(rs * qCutoff / np.pi)
 976    elif func == 'gaussian':
 977        rg = 1.0 / (qCutoff * np.sqrt(np.log(1.0 / gaussHeight) / 2.0))
 978        s = np.exp(-rs ** 2 / 2.0 / rg ** 2)
 979    else:
 980        print('The only function options are sinc and gaussian. Please check')
 981        print('your input. Using sinc by default.')
 982        s = np.sinc(rs * qCutoff / np.pi)
 983    xsmooth, ysmooth = cv(xdata, ydata, rs, s, align=True, normalize=True)
 984    return ysmooth
 985
 986
 987def getDiffData(fileName, fitIdx=0, writedata=False):
 988    """Extract the fit residual from a structural PDF fit. Works for .fgr and
 989       .ddp files.
 990
 991    Args:
 992        fileName (str): path to the .fgr or .ddp file containing the fit
 993        fitIdx (int): index of fit in .ddp file from which the residual
 994             is to be extracted.
 995        writedata (boolean): whether or not the output should be saved to file
 996
 997    Returns:
 998        r (numpy array): same r-grid as contained in the fit file
 999
1000        diff (numpy array): the structural PDF fit residual (i.e. the mPDF)
1001    """
1002    if fileName[-4:] == '.fgr':
1003        lines = open(fileName).readlines()[:50]
1004        for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
1005            if 'start data' in line:
1006                startLine = 1 * idx
1007                break
1008        allcols = np.loadtxt(fileName, unpack=True, comments='#', skiprows=startLine)
1009        r, diff = allcols[0], allcols[4]
1010        if writedata:
1011            np.savetxt(fileName[:-4] + '.diff', np.transpose((r, diff)))
1012        return r, diff
1013    elif fileName[-4:] == '.ddp':
1014        from diffpy.pdfgui import tui
1015        prj = tui.LoadProject(fileName)
1016        fit = prj.getFits()[fitIdx]
1017        dataSet = fit.getDataSet(0)
1018        r = np.array(dataSet.rcalc)
1019        diff = np.array(dataSet.Gdiff)
1020        if writedata:
1021            np.savetxt(fileName[:-4] + '_' + str(fitIdx) + '.diff',
1022                       np.transpose((r, diff)))
1023        return r, diff
1024    else:
1025        print('This file format is not currently supported.')
1026        return np.array([0]), np.array([0])
1027
1028def read_fgr(fileName):
1029    """Extract the PDF data and calculation from a .fgr file.
1030
1031    Args:
1032        fileName (str): path to the .fgr file containing the fit
1033
1034    Returns:
1035        r (numpy array): same r-grid as contained in the fit file
1036        gobs (numpy array): experimental PDF data
1037        gcalc (numpy array): the calculated PDF
1038        gdiff (numpy array): the structural PDF fit residual
1039    """
1040    if fileName[-4:] == '.fgr':
1041        lines = open(fileName).readlines()[:50]
1042        for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
1043            if 'start data' in line:
1044                startLine = 1 * idx
1045                break
1046        allcols = np.loadtxt(fileName, unpack=True, comments='#', skiprows=startLine)
1047        r, gcalc, gdiff = allcols[0], allcols[1], allcols[4]
1048        gobs = gcalc + gdiff
1049        return r, gobs, gcalc, gdiff
1050    else:
1051        print('Incompatible file type. Please provide a .fgr file from PDFgui.')
1052        return None

1054def calculateAvgB(struc):
1055    """Calculate average coherent neutron scattering length.
1056
1057    Args:
1058        struc: Diffpy Structure object
1059
1060    Returns:
1061        bAvg: average coherent neutron scattering length.
1062    """
1063    totalOcc = struc.occupancy.sum()
1064    bAvg = 0
1065    for idx, atom in enumerate(struc):
1066        el = re.findall("[a-zA-Z]+", atom.element)
1067        b = getattr(pt, el[0]).neutron.b_c
1068        bAvg += struc.occupancy[idx] * b
1069    bAvg /= totalOcc
1070    return bAvg
1071
1072def calculate_avg_spin_magnitude(magstruc, method='species'):
1073    """Calculate average spin magnitude from a MagStructure instance.
1074    
1075    Args:
1076        method (string): must be 'full' or 'species'. If 'full', the
1077            mean magnitude of all spins in the MagStructure will be
1078            returned. If 'species', then just a single spin from
1079            each species will be included in the calculation and weighted
1080            according to the species fraction. 'species' is faster and
1081            should be used if all spins belonging to a given species
1082            have the same magnitude.
1083    
1084    Returns: Mean magnitude of spins.
1085    """
1086    if method == 'species':
1087        try:
1088            magnitude = 0
1089            idx_dict = magstruc.getSpeciesIdxs()
1090            for key in magstruc.species:
1091                frac = magstruc.fractions[key]
1092                species_magnitude = np.linalg.norm(magstruc.spins[idx_dict[key]])
1093                magnitude += frac * species_magnitude
1094            return magnitude
1095        except:
1096            return np.mean(np.apply_along_axis(np.linalg.norm, 1, magstruc.spins))
1097    elif method == 'full':
1098        return np.mean(np.apply_along_axis(np.linalg.norm, 1, magstruc.spins))
1099    else:
1100        print("Please choose either 'species' or 'full' for the method.")
1101        print("Using 'full' for now.")
1102        return np.mean(np.apply_along_axis(np.linalg.norm, 1, magstruc.spins))
1103
1104def calculatemPDF(xyz, sxyz, gfactors=np.array([2.0]), calcIdxs=np.array([0]),
1105                  rstep=0.01, rmin=0.0, rmax=20.0, psigma=0.1, qmin=0,
1106                  qmax=-1, qdamp=0.0, extendedrmin=4.0, extendedrmax=4.0,
1107                  orderedScale=1.0,
1108                  K1=0.66667 * (GAMMA * r_0 / 2.0) ** 2 * 2.0 ** 2 * 0.5 * (0.5 + 1),
1109                  rho0=0, netMag=0, corrLength=0, linearTermMethod='exact',
1110                  applyEnvelope=False, qwindow=np.array([0]),
1111                  qgrid=np.array([0])):
1112    """Calculate the normalized mPDF.
1113
1114    At minimum, this module requires input lists of atomic positions and spins.
1115
1116    Args:
1117        xyz (numpy array): list of atomic coordinates of all the magnetic
1118            atoms in the structure.
1119        sxyz (numpy array): triplets giving the spin vectors of all the
1120            atoms, in the same order as the xyz array provided as input.
1121        gfactors (numpy array): Lande g-factors of spins in same order as
1122            spin array.
1123        calcIdxs (python list): list giving the indices of the atoms array
1124            specifying the atoms to be used as the origin when calculating
1125            the mPDF.
1126        rstep (float): step size for r-grid of calculated mPDF.
1127        rmin (float): minimum value of r for which mPDF should be calculated.
1128        rmax (float): maximum value of r for which mPDF should be calculated.
1129        psigma(float): std deviation (in Angstroms) of Gaussian peak
1130            to be convoluted with the calculated mPDF to simulate thermal
1131            motion.
1132        qmin (float): minimum experimentally accessible q-value (to be used
1133            for simulating termination ripples). If <0, no termination effects
1134            are included.
1135        qmax (float): maximum experimentally accessible q-value (to be used
1136            for simulating termination ripples). If <0, no termination effects
1137            are included.
1138        qdamp (float): usual PDF qdamp parameter. Turned off if set to zero.
1139        extendedrmin (float): extension of the r-grid on which the mPDF is
1140            calculated to properly account for contribution of pairs just
1141            before the boundary.
1142        extendedrmax (float): extension of the r-grid on which the mPDF is
1143            calculated to properly account for contribution of pairs just
1144            outside the boundary.
1145        ordScale (float): overall scale factor for the mPDF function f(r).
1146        K1 (float): A constant related to the total angular momentum quantum
1147            number and the average Lande splitting factor.
1148        rho0 (float): number of magnetic moments per cubic Angstrom in the
1149            magnetic structure; default value is 0.
1150        netMag (float): net magnetization in Bohr magnetons per magnetic moment
1151            in the sample; default is 0. Only nonzero for ferro/ferrimagnets or
1152            canted antiferromagnets.
1153        corrLength (float): exponential magnetic correlation length of the
1154            structure; default is 0, which is considered to be infinite.
1155            This is important to get the linear term right for samples
1156            with nonzero net magnetization.
1157        linearTermMethod (string): determines how the calculation will
1158            handle the linear term present for magnetic structures with a net
1159            magnetization. Options are:
1160            'exact'; slope will be calculated from the values of
1161                MagStructure.rho0 and MagStructure.netMag, damping set by
1162                MagStructure.corrLength.
1163            'autoslope': slope will be determined by least-squares
1164                minimization of the calculated mPDF, thereby ensuring that
1165                the mPDF oscillates around zero, as it is supposed to.
1166                Damping set by MagStructure.corrLength.
1167            'fullauto': slope and damping set by least-squares minimization.
1168                This should only be used in the case of an anisotropic
1169                correlation length.
1170            Note that any other option will be converted to 'exact'.
1171        applyEnvelope (boolean): if True, an exponential damping envelope will
1172            be applied to the calculated f(r) (not including the linear term).
1173            The parameter corrLength is used to determine the envelope.
1174        qwindow (numpy array): Q-space window function applied to the data
1175            prior to Fourier transformation. Not used by default.
1176        qgrid (numpy array): Q-space grid on which the window function is
1177            defined.
1178    Returns: numpy arrays for r and the mPDF fr, on the extended grid.
1179        """
1180    # check if g-factors have been provided
1181    if sxyz.shape[0] != gfactors.shape[0]:
1182        gfactors = 2.0 * np.ones(sxyz.shape[0])
1183    # calculate s1, s2
1184    r = np.arange(rmin - extendedrmin, rmax + extendedrmax + rstep, rstep)
1185    r = np.round(r, decimals=6)
1186    # don't calculate for negative r
1187    if r[0] < 0:
1188        startIdx = np.argmin(np.abs(r))
1189        if r[startIdx] < 0:
1190            startIdx += 1
1191        r = r[startIdx:]
1192    rbin = np.concatenate([r - rstep / 2, [r[-1] + rstep / 2]])
1193
1194    s1 = np.zeros(len(r))
1195    s2 = np.zeros(len(r))
1196
1197    if type(calcIdxs) is str:
1198        if calcIdxs == 'all':
1199            calcIdxs = np.arange(len(xyz))
1200
1201    for uu in calcIdxs:
1202        ri = xyz[uu]
1203        rj = xyz
1204        si = sxyz[uu]
1205        sj = sxyz
1206        gi = gfactors[uu]
1207        gj = gfactors
1208
1209        dxyz = rj - ri
1210        d2xyz = np.sum((dxyz) ** 2, axis=1).reshape(dxyz.shape[0], 1)
1211        d1xyz = np.sqrt(d2xyz)
1212        d1xyz[uu] = 1e-6  ### avoid divide by zero problem
1213        d1xyzr = d1xyz.ravel()
1214
1215        xh = dxyz / d1xyz
1216        yh = si - xh * np.sum(si * xh, axis=1).reshape(dxyz.shape[0], 1)
1217        yh_dis = np.sum(yh ** 2, axis=1)
1218        yh_ind = np.nonzero(np.abs(yh_dis) < 1e-10)
1219        yh[yh_ind] = [0, 0, 0]
1220        yh_dis[yh_ind] = 1e-6  ### avoid divide by zero problem
1221
1222        aij = np.sum(si * yh, axis=1) * np.sum(sj * yh, axis=1) / yh_dis
1223        aij[uu] = 0
1224        bij = 2 * np.sum(si * xh, axis=1) * np.sum(sj * xh, axis=1) - aij
1225
1226        w2 = bij / d1xyzr ** 3
1227
1228        d1xyzr[uu] = 0.0
1229        s1 += np.histogram(d1xyzr, bins=rbin, weights=gi * gj * aij)[0]
1230        s2 += np.histogram(d1xyzr, bins=rbin, weights=gi * gj * w2)[0]
1231
1232    # apply Gaussian shape function
1233    if psigma != None:
1234        x = np.arange(-3, 3, rstep)
1235        y = np.exp(-x ** 2 / psigma ** 2 / 2) * (1 / np.sqrt(2 * np.pi) / psigma)
1236
1237        s1[0] = 0
1238        s1 = fftconvolve(s1, y)
1239        s1 = s1[int(len(x) / 2): int(-len(x) / 2 + 1)]
1240
1241        s2 = fftconvolve(s2, y) * rstep
1242        s2 = s2[int(len(x) / 2): int(-len(x) / 2 + 1)]
1243
1244    ss2 = np.cumsum(s2)
1245
1246    if r[0] == 0:
1247        r[0] = 1e-4 * rstep  # avoid infinities at r = 0
1248        fr = s1 / r + r * (ss2[-1] - ss2)
1249        r[0] = 0
1250    else:
1251        fr = s1 / r + r * (ss2[-1] - ss2)
1252
1253    ### prefactor
1254    fr /= len(calcIdxs) * K1 / (GAMMA * r_0 / 2.0) ** 2
1255    if applyEnvelope and (corrLength != 0):
1256        fr *= np.exp(-r/corrLength)
1257
1258    ### Now include the linear term
1259    if linearTermMethod == 'autoslope':
1260        if corrLength == 0:
1261            def residual(p):
1262                return fr - p[0] * r
1263            opt = least_squares(residual, [0])
1264            linearTerm = opt.x[0] * r
1265        else:
1266            def residual(p):
1267                return fr - p[0] * r * np.exp(-r/corrLength)
1268            opt = least_squares(residual, [0])
1269            linearTerm = opt.x[0] * r * np.exp(-r/corrLength)
1270    elif linearTermMethod == 'fullauto':    
1271            def residual(p):
1272                return fr - p[0] * r * np.exp(-r/p[1])
1273            opt = least_squares(residual, [0, 100], bounds=[[-1e6,0], [1e6,1e6]])
1274            linearTerm = opt.x[0] * r * np.exp(-r/opt.x[1])
1275    else:
1276        if corrLength == 0:
1277            linearTerm = 4 * np.pi * r * rho0 * (2.0/3.0) * netMag**2  \
1278                         / ( K1 / (GAMMA * r_0 / 2.0) ** 2)
1279        else:
1280            linearTerm = 4 * np.pi * r * rho0 * (2.0 / 3.0) * netMag ** 2 * np.exp(-r/corrLength) \
1281                          / ( K1 / (GAMMA * r_0 / 2.0) ** 2)
1282    fr -= linearTerm
1283
1284
1285    ### apply the scale factor and qdamp
1286    fr *= orderedScale * np.exp((-1.0 * (qdamp * r) ** 2) / 2)
1287    # Do the convolution with the termination function if qmin/qmax or a window
1288    # function have been given
1289    if qmin >= 0 and qmax > qmin and len(qgrid) == 1: # no window function
1290        rth = np.arange(-rmax - extendedrmax, rmax + extendedrmax + rstep, rstep)
1291        th = (qmax/np.pi) * np.sinc(qmax * rth / np.pi) - (qmin / np.pi) * np.sinc(qmin * rth / np.pi)
1292        rcv, frcv = cv(r, fr, rth, th, align=True, normalize=True)
1293    elif len(qgrid) > 1: # use the window function
1294        rFT, windowFT = fourierTransform(qgrid, qwindow, rmin=-rmax, rmax=rmax, rstep=rstep)
1295        windowFT = np.real(windowFT)
1296        rcv, frcv = cv(r, fr, rFT, windowFT, align=True, normalize=True)
1297    else:
1298        rcv, frcv = r, fr
1299
1300    return rcv, frcv
1301
1302
1303def calculateDr(r, fr, q, ff, paraScale=1.0, rmintr=-5.0, rmaxtr=5.0,
1304                drtr=0.01, qmin=0, qmax=-1, K1=None, K2=None):
1305    """Calculate the unnormalized mPDF quantity D(r).
1306
1307    This module requires a normalized mPDF as an input, as well as a magnetic
1308    form factor and associated q grid.
1309
1310    Args:
1311        r (numpy array): r grid for the properly normalized mPDF.
1312        fr (numpy array): the properly normalized mPDF.
1313        q (numpy array): grid of momentum transfer values used for calculating
1314            the magnetic form factor.
1315        ff (numpy array): magnetic form factor. Same shape as ffqgrid.
1316        paraScale (float): scale factor for the paramagnetic part of the
1317            unnormalized mPDF function D(r).
1318        rmintr (float): minimum value of r for the Fourier transform of the
1319            magnetic form factor required for unnormalized mPDF.
1320        rmaxtr (float): maximum value of r for the Fourier transform of the
1321            magnetic form factor required for unnormalized mPDF.
1322        drtr (float): step size for r-grid used for calculating Fourier
1323            transform of magnetic form mactor.
1324        qmin (float): minimum experimentally accessible q-value (to be used
1325            for simulating termination ripples). If <0, no termination effects
1326            are included.
1327        qmax (float): maximum experimentally accessible q-value (to be used
1328            for simulating termination ripples). If <0, no termination effects
1329            are included.
1330        K1 (float): a constant used for calculating Dr; should be averaged
1331            over all magnetic species. Important if physical information is
1332            to be extracted from mPDF scale factors, e.g. moment size.
1333        K2 (float): another constant used for calculating Dr.
1334
1335    Returns: numpy array for the unnormalized mPDF Dr.
1336    """
1337    if K1 is None:
1338        K1 = 0.66667 * (GAMMA * r_0 / 2.0) ** 2 * 2.0 ** 2 * 0.5 * (0.5 + 1)
1339    if K2 is None:
1340        K2 = K1
1341    rsr, sr = cosTransform(q, ff, rmintr, rmaxtr, drtr)
1342    #### Double-check whether or not I should normalize sr!
1343    # norm = np.trapz(sr,rsr)
1344    # sr /= norm
1345    # sr = np.sqrt(np.pi/2.0)*sr ### I don't think we should multiply by sqrt(pi/2)
1346    rSr, Sr = cv(rsr, sr, rsr, sr)
1347    rDr, Dr = cv(r, K1 / (2.0 * np.pi) * fr, rSr, Sr)
1348    para = -K2 / np.pi * np.gradient(Sr, rSr[1] - rSr[0])  ### paramagnetic term in d(r)
1349    rpara, para = rSr, para
1350    # The code below is used to apply the termination convolution to the paramagnetic peak.
1351    # I don't think it's actually necessary.
1352#    if qmin >= 0 and qmax > qmin:
1353#        rstep = r[1] - r[0]
1354#        rth = np.arange(0.0, r.max() + rstep, rstep)
1355#        rth[0] = 1e-4 * rstep  # avoid infinities at r = 0
1356#        th = (np.sin(qmax * rth) - np.sin(qmin * rth)) / np.pi / rth
1357#        rth[0] = 0.0
1358#        rpara, para = cv(rSr, para, rth, th)
1359#    else:
1360#        rpara, para = rSr, para
1361    # make sure para and Dr match up in shape
1362    dr = r[2] - r[1]
1363    goodslice = np.logical_and(rDr >= r.min() - 0.5 * dr, rDr <= r.max() + 0.5 * dr)
1364    Dr = Dr[goodslice]
1365    para = para[rpara >= r.min() - 0.5 * dr]
1366    if para.shape[0] < Dr.shape[0]:
1367        para = np.concatenate((para, np.zeros(Dr.shape[0] - para.shape[0])))
1368    else:
1369        para = para[:Dr.shape[0]]
1370    Dr += paraScale * para
1371    return Dr
1372
1373
1374def calculateMagScatt(r, fr, qmin=0.0, qmax=20.0, qstep=0.01, quantity='sq'):
1375    """Calculate the magnetic scattering via Fourier transform of the mPDF.
1376
1377    Args:
1378        r (numpy array): r grid for the properly normalized mPDF.
1379        fr (numpy array): the mPDF, either normalized or unnormalized.
1380        qmin (float): minimum value of the output q-grid.
1381        qmax (float): maximum value of the output q-grid.
1382        qstep (float): spacing for the q-grid.
1383            unnormalized mPDF function D(r).
1384        quantity (str): type of magnetic scattering quantity to return; either
1385            'sq' or 'iq'. If 'sq', provide properly normalized mPDF; if 'iq',
1386            provide the unnormalized mPDF.
1387    Returns: q-grid and associated magnetic scattering.
1388    """
1389    if quantity == 'sq':
1390        q, fq = sinTransform(r, fr, qmin, qmax, qstep)
1391        sq = 1.0 * fq
1392        sq[1:] = fq[1:] / q[1:] + 1
1393        sq[0] = 0.0
1394        return q, sq
1395    elif quantity == 'iq':
1396        q, iqq = sinTransform(r, fr, qmin, qmax, qstep)
1397        iq = 1.0 * iqq
1398        iq[1:] = iq[1:] / q[1:]
1399        iq[0] = 0.0
1400        return q, iq
1401    else:
1402        print('Please specify a valid magnetic scattering type (sq or iq).')
1403        return 0 * r, 0 * fr

1406def calculate_ordered_moment(mc,nucScale,returnUncertainty=False,inputUnc=[]):
1407    """
1408    Calculate the ordered moment in Bohr magnetons determined from a fit.
1409    This only works for a magnetic structure with a single magnetic species.
1410    
1411    Args:
1412        mc: MPDFcalculator object used for the fit
1413        nucScale (float): nuclear scale factor determined from atomic PDF fit
1414        returnUncertainty (Boolean): If true, the uncertainty of the ordered
1415            moment will be estimated and returned.
1416        inputUnc (list): input uncertainties for mPDF ordered scale, nuclear
1417            scale factor, and correlation length, in that order.
1418
1419    Returns: ordered moment in Bohr magnetons. If the correlation length is
1420             finite, this yields the locally ordered moment at the nearest
1421             neighbor level. Also returns the estimated uncertainty if selected.
1422    """
1423    mstr = mc.magstruc
1424    struc = mstr.struc
1425    mstr.calcMagneticAtomRatio()
1426    ns = mstr.magneticAtomRatio # fraction of total atoms that are magnetic
1427    bAvg = calculateAvgB(struc) # average nuclear scattering length in fm
1428    bAvg /= 10.0 # convert to units of 10^-14 m
1429    g = mstr.gfactors[0] # g factor for the magnetic structrue
1430    vectorMag = np.linalg.norm(mstr.spins[0]) # magnitude of spin vectors used in calculation
1431    m = g * np.sqrt(mc.ordScale * bAvg**2 / (nucScale * ns)) * vectorMag
1432    if mstr.corrLength != 0:
1433        # find correlation length and nearest neighbor distance
1434        xi = mstr.corrLength
1435        rNN = np.min(np.apply_along_axis(np.linalg.norm, 1, mstr.atoms[1:] - mstr.atoms[0]))
1436        m *= np.exp(-rNN / 2.0 / xi)
1437    if returnUncertainty:
1438        d_mscl, d_nscl, d_xi = inputUnc
1439        # partial derivatives for error estimation
1440        dmdmscl = bAvg/np.sqrt(nucScale*ns*mc.ordScale)
1441        dmdnscl = -bAvg*np.sqrt(mc.ordScale/(ns*nucScale**3))
1442        if mstr.corrLength != 0:
1443            dmdxi = rNN*m/(2*xi**2)
1444        else:
1445            dmdxi = 0
1446        dm = np.sqrt(dmdmscl**2*d_mscl**2+dmdnscl**2*d_nscl**2+dmdxi**2*d_xi**2)
1447        return m, dm
1448    else:
1449        return m
1450
1451def calculate_ordered_scale(magstruc,orderedMoment,nucScale=1.0):
1452    """
1453    Calculate the ordered scale factor corresponding to a given ordered moment
1454    in Bohr magnetons. This only works for a magnetic structure with a single
1455    magnetic species. 
1456    
1457    Args:
1458        magstruc: MagStructure object
1459        orderedMoment (float): ordered moment in Bohr magnetons.
1460        nucScale (float): nuclear scale factor determined from atomic PDF fit.
1461                          Default value of 1.0
1462        
1463    Returns: Ordered scale factor corresponding to the given magnetic moment. If
1464             the correlation length is finite, this corresponds to the locally
1465             ordered moment at the nearest neighbor level.
1466    """
1467    struc = magstruc.struc
1468    magstruc.calcMagneticAtomRatio()
1469    ns = magstruc.magneticAtomRatio # fraction of total atoms that are magnetic
1470    bAvg = calculateAvgB(struc) # average nuclear scattering length
1471    bAvg /= 10.0 # convert to units of 10^-14 m
1472    g = np.mean(magstruc.gfactors) # g factor for the magnetic structrue
1473    vectorMag = calculate_avg_spin_magnitude(magstruc) # magnitude of spin vectors used in calculation
1474    oscl = (orderedMoment / g / vectorMag)**2 * nucScale * ns / bAvg**2 # ordered scale factor
1475    if magstruc.corrLength != 0:
1476        # find correlation length and nearest neighbor distance
1477        xi = magstruc.corrLength
1478        rNN = np.min(np.apply_along_axis(np.linalg.norm, 1, magstruc.atoms[1:] - magstruc.atoms[0]))
1479        oscl *= np.exp(rNN / xi)
1480    return oscl
1481
1482def compare_mPDF_nucPDF(mcif, rmin=0, rmax=20, ffparamkey='', qdamp=0.02,
1483              uiso=0.005, ordered_moment=-1):
1484    """Quick calculation of nuclear PDF and non-deconvoluted mPDF to scale.
1485
1486    Reads in an mcif to create the corresponding magnetic and atomic structures
1487    and calculates the mPDF and nuclear PDF to scale with each other for
1488    the purpose of comparing them.
1489    
1490    Args:
1491        mcif (string): file name of mcif containing the magnetic structure.
1492        rmin (float): minimum r value to be used in calculation. Default value
1493                      is 0.
1494        rmax (float): maximum r value to be used in calculation. Default value
1495                      is 20.
1496        ffparamkey (str): string specifying the magnetic form factor, e.g.
1497                          'Mn2' for Mn2+ or 'Fe3' for Fe3+. If left unspecified,
1498                          an average magnetic form factor will be used.
1499        qdamp (float): instrument resolution parameter. Default value 0.02.
1500        uiso (float): isotropic atomic displacement parameter. Default value 0.005.
1501        ordered_moment (float): magnitude of ordered moment in Bohr magnetons.
1502                                If left as the default -1, the length of the
1503                                spin vectors will be assumed to represent the
1504                                ordered moment.
1505    
1506    Returns:
1507        Python list containing the MPDFcalculator instance, r grid, deconvoluted
1508        mPDF, non-deconvoluted mPDF, and nuclear PDF.
1509
1510    """
1511    from diffpy.mpdf.mciftools import create_from_mcif
1512    from diffpy.mpdf.magstructure import MagStructure, MagSpecies
1513    from diffpy.mpdf.mpdfcalculator import MPDFcalculator
1514    mstruc = create_from_mcif(mcif, ffparamkey=ffparamkey,
1515                              rmaxAtoms=rmax)
1516    mstruc.Uiso = uiso
1517    mstruc.rmaxAtoms = rmax
1518    mstruc.makeAll()
1519    mstruc.calcNetMag()
1520    mstruc.calcAtomicDensity()
1521    if ordered_moment == -1:
1522        ordered_moment = calculate_avg_spin_magnitude(mstruc)
1523    scale = calculate_ordered_scale(mstruc, ordered_moment)
1524    mc = MPDFcalculator(mstruc, rmin=rmin, rmax=rmax, qdamp=qdamp,
1525                        ordScale=scale, paraScale=scale)
1526    r, g_mag, d_mag = mc.calc(both=True)
1527
1528    struc = mstruc.struc
1529    struc.Uisoequiv = uiso
1530    pc = PDFCalculator(scatteringfactortable='neutron', rmin=rmin,
1531                       rmax=rmax+0.00001, qdamp=qdamp) # fix indexing error
1532    r, g_nuc = pc(struc)
1533    return_items = [mc, r, g_mag, d_mag, g_nuc]
1534
1535    return return_items

1537def generate_damping_matrix(e1, e2, e3, xi1, xi2, xi3):
1538    """Generate the damping matrix from the eigenvectors and eigenvalues.
1539    
1540    Args:
1541        e1, e2, e3 (numpy arrays): right orthonormal eigenvectors
1542        xi1, xi2, xi3 (floats): correlation lengths along the directions
1543            of the eigenvectors
1544    
1545    Returns:
1546        dampingMat: 3x3 symmetric damping matrix.
1547    """
1548    m1 = np.array([e1,e2,e3]).T
1549    m2 = np.array([[1.0/xi1**2, 0, 0], [0, 1.0/xi2**2, 0], [0, 0, 1.0/xi3**2]])
1550    m3 = m1.T
1551    dampingMat = np.matmul(np.matmul(m1, m2), m3)
1552    return dampingMat
1553
1554def estimate_effective_xi(dampingMat, N=1000):
1555    """
1556    Estimate the effective correlation length for a given damping matrix. 
1557    
1558    Determines the correlation length for a given number of randomly generated
1559    direction vectors, then calculates the weighted average where the weights
1560    are given by the volume of the damping matrix ellipsoid subtended by each
1561    direction vector.
1562    Note: This is somewhat of an experimental function, not yet rigorously
1563    shown to be correct.
1564
1565    Args:
1566        dampingMat (numpy array): 3x3 damping matrix corresponding to a
1567            (potentially) anisotropic correlation length.
1568        N (int): number of random directions to average over. Default is 1000.
1569        
1570    Returns: estimated effective correlation length.
1571    """
1572    # put matrix in diagonal form
1573    ev = np.linalg.eig(dampingMat)[0]
1574    dampingMat = np.array([[ev[0],0,0],[0,ev[1],0],[0,0,ev[2]]])
1575    # generate uniform sampling of direction
1576    ths = np.arccos(np.random.uniform(-1, 1, size=N))
1577    phis = np.random.uniform(-np.pi, np.pi, size=N)
1578    x = np.sin(ths)*np.cos(phis)
1579    y = np.sin(ths)*np.sin(phis)
1580    z = np.cos(ths)
1581    randomVecs = np.transpose((x, y, z))
1582    # calculate correlation length along each direction
1583    mult1 = np.tensordot(dampingMat, randomVecs, axes=(0,1)).T
1584    xi = 1.0/np.sqrt(np.apply_along_axis(np.sum, 1, randomVecs*mult1))
1585    # generate weights according to volume subtended by each direction vector
1586    weights = xi**5 * np.sin(ths)
1587    return np.sum(weights * xi)/np.sum(weights)
1588
1589def gauss(grid,s=0.5):
1590    """Generate a gaussian kernel of arbitrary size and density
1591    This function generates a 3D guassian kernel based on the input grid and the standard
1592    deviation chosen. This is a simple replacement for the form factors that will be
1593    implemented in the future.
1594    Args:
1595        grid (array): the 3D spatial coordinates for the gaussian kernel
1596        s (float): The standard deviation for the gaussian kernel
1597    """
1598    g = lambda point: 1/(s*np.sqrt((2*np.pi*s)**3))*np.exp(-1/2*(np.linalg.norm(point)/s)**2)
1599    return np.apply_along_axis(g,3,grid)

1601def vec_ac(a1,a2,delta,corr_mode="same"):
1602    """Correlate two 3D vector fields
1603    This function computes the autocorrelation of two 3D vector fields on regular 
1604    grids. The autocorrelation is computed for each vector component and then summed
1605    Args:
1606        a1 (array): The virst array to correlate
1607        a2 (array): The second array to correlate
1608        delta (float): the spacing between grid points
1609        corr_mode (string): The mode to use for the scipy correlation function
1610    """
1611    ac = correlate(a1[:,:,:,0],a2[:,:,:,0],mode=corr_mode)*delta**3
1612    ac += correlate(a1[:,:,:,1],a2[:,:,:,1],mode=corr_mode)*delta**3
1613    ac += correlate(a1[:,:,:,2],a2[:,:,:,2],mode=corr_mode)*delta**3
1614    return ac
1615
1616def vec_con(a1,a2,delta,conv_mode="same"):
1617    """Implement convolution for 3D vector fields
1618    This function implements a convolution function for 3D vector fields on regular 
1619    grids. The convolution is computed for each component of the vector fields and summed
1620    Args:
1621        a1 (array): The first array to convolve
1622        a2 (array): The second array to convolve
1623        delta (float): The grid spacing
1624        conv_mode (string): The mode to use for scipy convolution
1625    """
1626    con = convolve(a1[:,:,:,0],a2[:,:,:,0],mode=conv_mode)*delta**3
1627    con += convolve(a1[:,:,:,1],a2[:,:,:,1],mode=conv_mode)*delta**3
1628    con += convolve(a1[:,:,:,2],a2[:,:,:,2],mode=conv_mode)*delta**3
1629    return con

1631def ups(grid):
1632    """A function to generat the Upsilon filter from Roth et.al. (2018)
1633    This function computes an kernel using the upsilon function defined in Roth et.al.
1634    (2018), https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052252518006590.
1635    Args:
1636        grid (array): the spatial grid over which the kernel is to be defined
1637    """
1638    g = lambda point: [0,0,0] if np.abs(np.linalg.norm(point)) <1e-6 else  point/np.linalg.norm(point)**4
1639    return np.apply_along_axis(g,3,grid)
1640    
1641def calculate_g_factors(S, L, J):
1642    """A function to calculate the Lande g factor and the spin and orbital
1643    components gS and gL.
1644    
1645    Args:
1646        S (float): Spin angular momentum quantum number in units of hbar.
1647        L (float): Orbital angular momentum quantum number in units of hbar.
1648        J (float): Total angular momentum quantum number in units of hbar.
1649
1650    Returns:
1651        gS: spin component of Lande g factor
1652        gL: orbital component of Lande g factor
1653        g: total Lande g factor
1654    """
1655    gS = 1.0 + 1.0*(S*(S+1)-L*(L+1))/(J*(J+1))
1656    gL = 0.5 + 1.0*(L*(L+1)-S*(S+1))/(2*J*(J+1))
1657    g = gS + gL
1658    return gS, gL, g
GAMMA = 1.913
r_0 = 0.281794
def generateAtomsXYZ(struc, rmax=30.0, strucIdxs=[0], square=False): 
37def generateAtomsXYZ(struc, rmax=30.0, strucIdxs=[0], square=False):
38    """Generate array of atomic Cartesian coordinates from a given structure.
39
40    Args:
41        struc (diffpy.Structure object): provides lattice parameters and unit
42            cell of the desired structure
43        rmax (float): largest distance from central atom that should be
44            included
45        strucIdxs (python list): list of integers giving indices of magnetic
46            atoms in the unit cell
47        square (boolean): if not True, atoms within a given radius from the
48            origin will be returned; if True, then the full grid will be
49            returned rather than just a spherical selection.
50
51    Returns:
52        numpy array of triples giving the Cartesian coordinates of all the
53            magnetic atoms. Atom closest to the origin placed first in array.
54
55    Note: If square = True, this may have problems for structures that have
56        a several distorted unit cell (i.e. highly non-orthorhombic).
57    """
58    if not square:
59        magAtoms = struc[strucIdxs]
60        bc = BondCalculator(rmax=rmax + np.linalg.norm(struc.lattice.stdbase.sum(axis=1)))
61        bc.setPairMask(0, 'all', True, others=False)
62        bc(magAtoms)
63        r0 = struc.xyz_cartn[strucIdxs[0]]
64        atoms = np.vstack([r0, r0 + bc.directions[bc.sites0 == 0]])
65
66    else:
67        ### generate the coordinates of each unit cell
68        lat = struc.lattice
69        unitcell = lat.stdbase
70        cellwithatoms = struc.xyz_cartn[np.array(strucIdxs)]
71        dim1 = int(np.round(rmax / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[0])))
72        dim2 = int(np.round(rmax / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[1])))
73        dim3 = int(np.round(rmax / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[2])))
74        ocoords = np.mgrid[-dim1:dim1 + 1, -dim2:dim2 + 1, -dim3:dim3 + 1].transpose().ravel().reshape(
75            (2 * dim1 + 1) * (2 * dim2 + 1) * (2 * dim3 + 1), 3)
76        latos = np.dot(ocoords, unitcell)
77
78        ### rearrange latos array so that [0, 0, 0] is the first one (for convenience)
79        latos[np.where(np.all(latos == [0, 0, 0], axis=1))] = latos[0]
80        latos[0] = np.array([0, 0, 0])
81
82        ### create list of all atomic positions
83        atoms = np.empty([len(latos) * len(cellwithatoms), 3])
84        index = 0
85        for lato in latos:
86            for atompos in cellwithatoms:
87                atoms[index] = lato + atompos
88                index += 1
89
90    return atoms

Generate array of atomic Cartesian coordinates from a given structure.

Args: struc (diffpy.Structure object): provides lattice parameters and unit cell of the desired structure rmax (float): largest distance from central atom that should be included strucIdxs (python list): list of integers giving indices of magnetic atoms in the unit cell square (boolean): if not True, atoms within a given radius from the origin will be returned; if True, then the full grid will be returned rather than just a spherical selection.

Returns: numpy array of triples giving the Cartesian coordinates of all the magnetic atoms. Atom closest to the origin placed first in array.

Note: If square = True, this may have problems for structures that have a several distorted unit cell (i.e. highly non-orthorhombic).

def generateSpinsXYZ( struc, atoms=array([], shape=(1, 0), dtype=float64), kvecs=array([[0, 0, 0]]), basisvecs=array([[0, 0, 1]]), origin=array([0, 0, 0]), avgmom=array([0, 0, 0])): 
 93def generateSpinsXYZ(struc, atoms=np.array([[]]), kvecs=np.array([[0, 0, 0]]),
 94                     basisvecs=np.array([[0, 0, 1]]), origin=np.array([0, 0, 0]),
 95                     avgmom=np.array([0, 0, 0])):
 96    """Generate array of 3-vectors representing the spins in a structure.
 97
 98    Args:
 99        struc (diffpy.Structure object): provides lattice parameters and unit
100            cell of the desired structure
101        atoms (numpy array): list of atomic coordinates of all the magnetic
102            atoms of a given magnetic species in the structure
103        avgmom (numpy array): three-vector giving the average moment for the
104            magnetic species.
105        kvecs (numpy array): list of three-vectors giving the propagation
106            vector(s) of the magnetic structure
107        basisvecs (numpy array): list of three-vectors describing the spin
108            located at the spin origin.
109        origin (numpy array): Cartesian coordinates specifying the origin
110            to be used when calculating the phases of the spins.
111
112    Returns:
113        numpy array of triples giving the spin vectors of all the magnetic
114            atoms, in the same order as the atoms array provided as input.
115
116    """
117
118    lat = struc.lattice
119    rlat = lat.reciprocal()
120    (astar, bstar, cstar) = (rlat.cartesian((1, 0, 0)), rlat.cartesian((0, 1, 0)),
121                             rlat.cartesian((0, 0, 1)))
122    i = 1j
123
124    spins = 0 * atoms
125    cspins = 0 * atoms + 0j * atoms
126    if len(np.array(kvecs).shape) == 1:
127        kvecs = [kvecs]
128    if len(np.array(basisvecs).shape) == 1:
129        basisvecs = [basisvecs]
130    for idx, kvec in enumerate(kvecs):
131        kcart = kvec[0] * astar + kvec[1] * bstar + kvec[2] * cstar
132        phasefac = np.exp(-2.0 * np.pi * i * np.dot(atoms - origin, kcart))
133        cspins += basisvecs[idx] * phasefac[:, np.newaxis]
134    cspins += avgmom
135    spins = np.real(cspins)
136
137    if np.abs(np.imag(cspins)).max() > 0.0001:
138        print((np.abs(np.imag(cspins)).max()))
139        print('Warning: basis vectors resulted in complex spins.')
140        print('Imaginary parts have been discarded.')
141
142    return spins

Generate array of 3-vectors representing the spins in a structure.

Args: struc (diffpy.Structure object): provides lattice parameters and unit cell of the desired structure atoms (numpy array): list of atomic coordinates of all the magnetic atoms of a given magnetic species in the structure avgmom (numpy array): three-vector giving the average moment for the magnetic species. kvecs (numpy array): list of three-vectors giving the propagation vector(s) of the magnetic structure basisvecs (numpy array): list of three-vectors describing the spin located at the spin origin. origin (numpy array): Cartesian coordinates specifying the origin to be used when calculating the phases of the spins.

Returns: numpy array of triples giving the spin vectors of all the magnetic atoms, in the same order as the atoms array provided as input.

def generateFromUnitCell(unitcell, atombasis, spinbasis, rmax=30.0): 
145def generateFromUnitCell(unitcell, atombasis, spinbasis, rmax=30.0):
146    """Generate array of atomic Cartesian coordinates from a given structure.
147
148    Args:
149        unitcell (numpy array): np.array([avec, bvec, cvec])
150        atombasis (numpy array): gives positions of magnetic atoms in
151            fractional coordinates; np.array([pos1, pos2, pos3, ...])
152        spinbasis (numpy array): gives orientations of the magnetic moments
153            in the unit cell, in the same order as atombasis
154        rmax (float): largest distance from central atom that should be
155            included
156
157    Returns:
158        atoms = numpy array of triples giving the Cartesian coordinates of all
159              the magnetic atoms. Atom closest to the origin placed first in
160              array.
161        spins = numpy array of triples giving the Cartesian coordinates of all
162              the spins in the structure, in the same order as atoms.
163
164    Note: This will only work well for structures that can be expressed with a
165        unit cell that is close to orthorhombic or higher symmetry.
166    """
167    if len(np.array(atombasis).shape) == 1:
168        atombasis = [atombasis]
169    if len(np.array(spinbasis).shape) == 1:
170        spinbasis = [spinbasis]
171    cellwithatoms = np.dot(atombasis, unitcell)  ### check this
172    radius = rmax + 15.0
173    dim1 = int(np.round(radius / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[0])))
174    dim2 = int(np.round(radius / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[1])))
175    dim3 = int(np.round(radius / np.linalg.norm(unitcell[2])))
176
177    ### generate the coordinates of each unit cell
178    ocoords = np.mgrid[-dim1:dim1 + 1, -dim2:dim2 + 1, -dim3:dim3 + 1].transpose().ravel().reshape(
179        (2 * dim1 + 1) * (2 * dim2 + 1) * (2 * dim3 + 1), 3)
180    latos = np.dot(ocoords, unitcell)
181
182    ### select points within a desired radius from origin
183    latos = latos[np.where(np.apply_along_axis(np.linalg.norm, 1, latos) <=
184                           (rmax + np.linalg.norm(unitcell.sum(axis=1))))]
185
186    ## rearrange latos array so that [0, 0, 0] is the first one (for convenience)
187    latos[np.where(np.all(latos == [0, 0, 0], axis=1))] = latos[0]
188    latos[0] = np.array([0, 0, 0])
189
190    ### create list of all atomic positions
191    atoms = np.empty([len(latos) * len(cellwithatoms), 3])
192    spins = np.empty_like(atoms)
193    index = 0
194    for lato in latos:
195        for j, atompos in enumerate(cellwithatoms):
196            atoms[index] = lato + atompos
197            spins[index] = spinbasis[j]
198            index += 1
199    return atoms, spins
